## Now

By the project's direction the work does not stop. A batch that ends is followed by the next item in
the order under the head with no wait for a reply; global illumination is fixed first (Decision 74),
the meadow at 8:00 the one target (Decision 81).

1. **What the next page says.** Each push's run and each pack run is read by the reviewing session
    from GitHub's API, and a failure it names is a verdict here and comes first. The runs' record
    since the bump stands in REVIEW-ARCHIVE.md under Items closed, parked or shortened, with this
    item as it stood.

    reads the lists for the files it will touch before it starts. Every ask the item held has
    landed, N 1.3's Slang count among them in NormTests.cs; the record stands in REVIEW-ARCHIVE.md
    under Items closed, parked or shortened.

    door after a delay and once. After item 65.

67. **The level editor edits the file in Hammer's four panes or Unreal's single view, switchable.**
    From Decision 61, level editing for artists who do not program. The editor opens a level file,
    shows it in four panes, the view and the top, front and side, or in one view, switched by a key,
    draws brushes with a block tool, moves their faces and vertices, applies textures with the
    world-aligned mapping, places entities and edits their keyvalues, and holds the connections of
    item 66 in a panel of outputs, targets, inputs, parameters, delays and fire once; it saves the
    file the engine loads. Phases proposed by the coder; after item 66. The coder's phases are four
    panes or one view, switchable, with a power-of-two grid; the block tool, select, move and resize
    with snapping, undo and saving; the clip tool, vertex editing kept convex and face texturing;
    entities, their properties and item 66's connections panel.

## Verdicts

No verdict is open. Verdicts 2 and 33 to 59 are settled, said under each in REVIEW-ARCHIVE.md.

## Decisions

Decisions 1 Commits stay local; 2 AGENTS.md's bullet on SHARED.md changes by the project's direction
alone; 3 A picture opens the example's own source, and not Bevy's live demo of it; 4 AGENTS.md's
bullet on NORM.md changes by the project's direction alone, with the exception N 7.4 makes; 5 The
examples written are brought to B 4 a group at a time; 6 A run that fails says what failed in a
page, and the reviewing session is given no log; 7 The page's repeated lines are warnings and
errors; 8 The next package is 0.4; 9 A document a game's author reads names no one who decided; 10
The tests run on macOS as well; 11 Feathers' crate may be enabled, after the other gaps; 12 The free
and pan camera controllers may be enabled, after the other gaps; 13 System font discovery stays off;
14 The sample becomes a feature test; 15 Graphics test scenes come as packs fetched on demand, never
checked in; 16 Every tonemapper here comes to 3DEngine; 17 The embedding is the bridge's own; 18 The
weather is vendored and ported; 19 Bevy 0.20 comes after the deferred batch in flight and before the
other gaps; 20 The crates' word for the upgrade; 21 No document or comment a reader sees names a
person or a session; 22 Content streamed on the go stays in the ledger, and the browser stays out;
23 A run that shows no window makes no sound; 24 A game's session writes what the engine lacks in
`.github/ASKS.md`, here as in 3DEngine; 25 A feature of a crate already in the tree that pulls no
crate in is the working session's to turn on; a feature that pulls a crate in waits on the owner's

80. **No millisecond budget.** Decided on 2026-11-08 at 08:50. There is no millisecond budget. A
   feature is first made to work and to perform well, and its numbers are worked on after or along
   the way as much as possible. So a mend that brings a view to its reference lands by its figures,
   its cost measured and recorded beside them and cut after or along the way where a cut holds the
   readings; item 114 and the rest land or stay by their figures, the cost a figure and not a gate,
   and the forest's and the meadow's milliseconds stay in each record.

81. **A stop rule and one target.** On 2026-11-08 at 08:5x, on the question why the light leaking
   had moved little in days, the direction was that the review does what it thinks right and reports
   it for approval. Approved at 08:49 on 2026-11-08, so a view inside its band lands and a figure
   that remains is recorded and not chased unless it lies in a scene that is looked at, the meadow
   here and Sponza's named views in the engine; one bounded read places a cause and a second is the
   last before a mend is tried or the figure recorded. The meadow at eight in the morning is the
   bridge's one target scene, its crowns and its grass against the one reference, the rooms the
   guard.

83. **Version tags.** Decided at about 14:00 on 2026-11-08, after every commit of the Unity
    Essentials repositories was tagged as `v2.0.30` and the like, the three projects take tags too,
    with the review's questions answered at 14:1x. The form is `v6.0.91`, the letter v before
    `build/version.sh`'s number. Tags go on each major or minor change and on the commits packages
    were built from, since a tag on every commit clutters the list and is unnecessary, the tags
    marking releases some time apart with meaningful changes and not commits apart. The major and
    the minor are the sessions' to raise, each session working on the project deciding when the time
    is right to raise the minor or the major, every commit counting as a patch, with full liberty
    once a step is done and meaningful changes were made. N 6.3 holds the rule and the reviewer sets
    the tags as it pushes. `v0.6.0` marks the commit that set 0.6 and `v0.6.18` the commit
    `b8cc8316` the package of 0.6.18 was published from on 2026-11-02, both set at 14:12.

84. **No middle dot.** Decided at 17:57 and 18:00 on 2026-11-08, the middle dot is not used, the
    README's top links separated by a space alone and the dot nowhere else; the reviewer changed the
    README's first line in the tree on that decision, for the next commit to carry, and every other
    middle dot in the repository is item 118's. The rule goes into STYLE.md's Punctuation as the
    shared text has it everywhere.

85. **One repository, many projects.** The engines' future was thought through with the review at
    about 18:20 on 2026-11-08, after Unity Essentials, where every feature is a repository of its
    own. The points made were that the engines are somewhat cluttered and should be modular,
    extendable, stable and easy to use, that splitting everything into repositories adds clutter and
    makes commits awkward, that the shared modules' repositories are right, that the engine's own
    content could be made modular the same way inside its repository, and that one running process,
    edited and seen as it changes, is worth thinking about; the review's recommendation was approved
    at 18:30. The direction is that each engine stays one repository and becomes one solution of
    many projects, each an area with its own public surface and its own plugin, packed as its own
    package at one version for all, as Bevy's crates are in Bevy's one repository; the dependency
    direction is held by project references and a norm test over them; the flat API stays unchanged
    on top and a game names the packages it needs; the names are dotted .NET names and not com.;
    there is no editor, and the live path is a watcher that recompiles a changed shader, reloads a
    changed asset or scene and recompiles a changed behavior into the running process, the engine's
    own code by restart. It is scheduled after the current items and done as one mechanical batch
    per engine with the public API held identical before and after and the documents' tables
    redrawn. Items 119 and 120, 3DEngine Decision 102.

86. **Comments on the code's own terms.** A comment of scenes_sponza was read at about 19:00 on
    2026-11-08, "The frame graded as that scene's HDRP profile grades it, by the look of its AgX -
    Powerful.exr, a lookup build/unity-lut.py writes from that strip, a gamma of w 0.225, and a
    bloom of intensity 0.25, threshold 0.333 and scatter 0.7, worked out as HDRP works them out",
    and found to read badly, to read as an em dash does, and to lean too far on outside knowledge
    and on the sessions' knowledge of work in progress, in scenes_sponza explicitly and probably
    everywhere else. The rule from it, in STYLE.md's Register and as N 4.11, is that a comment
    stands on the code's own terms. It says what the code does and why in the engine's words; a
    number taken from elsewhere stands with the reason it is right here, what it makes the frame or
    the program do, and the source is named once in the documents' references and not in the
    comment; the file names of outside assets, another product's profile or process as the
    explanation, "as X works it out", and the facts of the sessions' work are not written in a
    comment. Item 121, 3DEngine Decision 103.

    comment on the far cascade of 100 that carried the lion's end wall's reading from 34.6 to 15.1
    times its reference and the mend's 0.6 ms, a comment need not name the progress or the
    millisecond count, a comment being no protocol. N 4.11 widens so that a comment carries no
    reading of before and after, no cost figure and no account of the trials, which are the review's
    records and RENDERING.md's; a number stands in a comment only where the code's choice depends on

88. **One package on nuget.org.** Chosen on 2026-11-11 at about 16:20, on the review's question with
    the twenty ids of item 119's split laid out, BevyCSharp keeps one package, since so many
    different packages are a burden, are not good and are not necessary, and for both engines the
    preference is one package alone, or two with the second holding heavy binaries. So the library's
    areas stay projects of their own inside the repository, their layers held by the project
    references and N 1.6, and BevyCSharp's one package carries every area's assembly, the modules',
    the six systems' bridges, the analyzers and the build files; no BevyCSharp.<Area> id is
    published. Asked about the bridge's size, 249.9 MB against nuget.org's limit of 250, the choice
    was to keep one package there too. The pack job says the package's size and fails before the
    push where it is over the limit. Decision 85's packages at one version give way to this for the
    bridge. Asked again at about 16:40 between one package and two, the second for the bridges under
    a name such as BevyCSharp.Binaries as had been suggested, the choice was one package with the
    bridge shrunk, a second package of the bridges alone standing at about 247 MB of the limit by

    question, among this, two copies with a check of their parity, and one engine's lighting alone.
    The kernels of the radiance cascades stand twice, here and in the sibling, ported by hand, and
    two faults of one night, the glow history's quarter texel and the depth's points far from the

90. **An editor as a module both engines use, later.** The direction of 2026-11-12 is that the
    editor is no focus yet and will be. The aim is a full framework in which ImGui frames for editor
    tools are built easily, with helpers that show data such as the ECS and assets in diagnostics
    windows and a way for a shell to have a surface for an editor layout, a module used by both
    engines, made in ImGui as this library's is, giving an engine the functions to build an editor
    on or a way to show its data in one. It is thought through further before it is taken up, so no
    item is made and nothing is moved. BevyCSharp.Editor stands as it is, its shell owning the
    arrangement and its panels registered in tables, and the two engines stay on one ImGui binding
    at one version. Added the same morning, of how it sits and of what there is. The editor module
    provides functions and drawing calls that the engine uses in its own ImGui scope, in the same
    process and as ImGui calls alone. So the engine hosts, the module owning no window, no ImGui
    context and no process. This library's editor is not taken as the module's design; it is
    progress to learn from, and the module's own design is set out when the module is taken up.

a private field, a text in a private auto-property, a note in a struct marked Hidden and words in

began. GeneratorAttributeTests.AHandleNoHookCanReachIsSaid holds a text in a private struct and

146's medium findings 21 to 24, the export's bridge and three tests that passed on broken code, in

An export builds its render bridge again when the one it built before is older than any file the
bridge is built from, the list the library's build holds a staged bridge to, everything under the
crate's sources but their tests and fixtures, the crate's Cargo.toml and build.rs, and the
workspace's Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock, where it looked at the Rust sources and the crate's
Cargo.toml alone. EditorPlayTests.ABridgeOlderThanAnythingItIsBuiltFromIsBuiltAgain makes each file
newer than the library in turn. Without the mend, the old inputs behind the overload the test calls,
a shader made newer left the bridge current and a test's file made it stale, and the old inputs hold
neither the build script nor the workspace's files. With it each file the bridge is built from makes
it stale, and the tests and fixtures do not. The test is listed in build/norm/1.4.txt beside the
editor's other tests, by its nature, as the list's head allows for a test of what is no area of the
library.

The three tests are made to fail on the code broken as each finding says, each run on that code as
it was and as it is, and on the code as it is.
OtherComponentTests.EachEntityMovesItsOwnTransformAndTheWholeSetCrossesAFewTimes holds that the

StreamingTests.FinishedReadsAreHandedOverWithinTheBudget asks for the low read before the high one

0.8 and 1.4. With a Change that leaves an armed timer as it was, the test as it was passed and as it

146's medium findings 30 and 31, physics' bounce and the spatial scale, in the commit carrying this
Reply.

Two touching bodies bounce as the bouncier of the two does, as the guide and PhysicsMaterial say,
each dynamic body of the pair struck with the pair's bounce, where only a dynamic body whose own
material was bouncy bounced, and by its own. The speed a body came into the step with is recorded
for every awake dynamic body while anything in the world is bouncy, and for none in a world with
nothing bouncy. BounceTests.ATouchingPairBouncesAsTheBouncierOfTheTwo drops a ball of no bounce and
one of 0.3 on pads of 0.9, and a ball of no bounce on a dull floor. Without the mend the dull ball
on the bouncy pad came back up only to 0.59 of a unit, where the test asks for more than 2.1, and
with it the test passes, as do the physics, contact, sleep and kinematic body classes beside it, 44
in all. docs/physics.md says a bouncy pad throws back a crate of no bounce of its own.

Config.SpatialScale is said as what a world unit is multiplied by to give meters, 0.01 for a world
measured in centimeters or pixels, since Bevy multiplies the sound's and the ears' positions by it,
where it said a hundred. It is a comment alone, which no test reads.

The whole suite that passed over these is the one the asset fields' Reply above gives. NormTests
passed, 19.

143, the read of the tests that need a renderer on the render bridge under lavapipe held to four
cores, in the commit carrying this Reply, with the mends of three tests the read found at fault, and
the plan of the Linux job's parts by minutes, which comes in a commit after it.

The 172 classes whose tests call Needs.Shaders, 58, or Needs.Renderer alone, 114, ran on the pack
run's render bridge for linux-x64 in a container of the runner's image, Ubuntu 24.04 with Mesa
25.2.8, lavapipe held to four cores by LP_NUM_THREADS and by taskset inside the container. The suite
was built in that image, and Mesa's shader cache started empty and was kept from class to class, as
a job's would be. Each class was a build/test.py run of its own in a container of its own, killed at
a quarter hour, under the GPU lock shared once no exclusive lock had been held or waiting for three
minutes, so a timing got in between any two. The seven readings of a cost in a forest or a room were
left out, each drawing hundreds of frames at 1080p to time a GPU's passes, which tells nothing of a
device that draws on the processor.

A piece is one case, or a few cases of one class packed by their earlier times under the cap, run as
a class is, a test.py run in a container of its own. 168 classes ran whole, and 5 of them, four of
the trees' classes and the wind's, ran past the quarter hour, their cases that ended counted from
that run and the rest dealt into pieces. The other 4, the bounce rooms', the reference's, global
illumination's and the canopy's, were set aside as too long for one run and read in pieces alone. So
9 classes came to 93 pieces. 11 of them ran past the quarter hour and 2 lost their cases to a filter
MSBuild could not read, a theory case's quoted argument, and those 13 ran again a case at a time,
held to 41 minutes, of which 10 ended and 3 ran past it.

The 114 classes that need a renderer alone take 46 minutes of processes, 40 of them in their cases.
The 58 that need shaders take 562 minutes, 436 of them in their cases, global illumination's class
242 alone. 21 of their cases take five minutes or more each, 247 minutes together, each a reading
against a traced reference, a forest or a tree between its levels, and the thousand-tree forest of
TreeMemoryTests takes 24 minutes. Three cases ran out the 41 minutes,
GlobalIlluminationTests.ProbesAboutAFrontLitCrownHoldTheLightItsLeavesScatter,
GlobalIlluminationTests.ALoneAspenLitFromBehindLetsThroughTheSunItsReferenceDoes and
TreeWindTests.AWindBendsATreeDownwindAndTwoTreesAlikeSwayOutOfStep, which take 19.6, 12.7 and 22.8
seconds on the card, more than a hundred times as long here, where the lone aspen under the sky
takes 631 seconds against the card's 16. 1,161 cases passed, 3 failed and 22 were skipped, 12 of
them Solari's and 4 the meshlets', which the pack's render bridge is built without, and 6 needing
what the image lacks, a sound device, Feathers' source in the cargo registry, the examples'
textures, Python 3.14 for build/textures.py in two, and a headless bridge.

SpirvComputeTests.ARaySceneOfItsOwnIsTracedAndFollowsWhatMoves failed, the slab met by no ray. A
trial laid the scene five ways, and the slab is met in slot 1 of 2, in slot 1 of 4 with the
stand-ins after it, alone in slot 0, and in slot 3 with real cubes far off in slots 1 and 2, and
missed only in slot 3 with the stand-ins of mask zero in slots 1 and 2. The Vulkan specification has
an instance whose mask shares no bit with the ray's cull mask never met, and says nothing more of a
mask of zero, so the fault is lavapipe's. The test lays the slab in slot 1 on a CPU device, the
stand-ins after it, so ray four still passes through the stand-in at the origin and finds it never
met, and keeps slot 3 everywhere else, where the slot the empty ones leave as it was is held.
docs/ray-tracing.md says a scene meant to be traced on lavapipe fills its slots from zero. In a copy
of the read's tree from a Mesa cache that started empty, the test as it was failed on lavapipe as
the read had it, and mended it passes there and on the card.

A report for Mesa, drafted and not filed. Lavapipe in Mesa 25.2.8 commits no hit on an instance of a
top-level acceleration structure laid after instances whose mask is zero. A structure of four
instances, a cube in instance 0, the same cube with mask 0 in instances 1 and 2 at the origin, and a
slab of mask 0xFF in instance 3, traced with rayQueryInitializeEXT and a cull mask of 0xFF straight
down onto the slab, commits nothing, where the slab in instance 1 with the instances of mask 0 after
it, or in instance 3 with instances of mask 0xFF in 1 and 2 placed away from the rays, is met. An
instance of mask 0 is never met by the specification, which makes nothing of the instances after it.

GlobalIlluminationTests.ALoneAspensLeavesUnderAUniformSkyReadTheirReference read +28% against its
bound of 25%, where the card reads +24% on the same reference, 0.0471 on both. A trial wrote the
picture at Medium, the picture with global illumination off and the reference whole on both devices.
The reference, the floor and the stems read alike, the floor within 0.2% and the stems within about
1%, and the leaves read 3.0% higher on lavapipe at Medium and 3.6% with global illumination off, so
it is neither the probes nor their rays. It grows with the slant, 2.4% on the leaves that face the
eye and 5 to 10% on those seen side on, and the leaves' textures are filtered with sixteen samples
at a slant. With one sample on both devices the two read alike within 0.2%, 0.0599 and 0.0600, and
to the fourth place with global illumination off. On the card the sixteen samples take 3.1 points
off the test's +27.2%, and on lavapipe 0.3, so the leaves read 27% over their reference with their
textures filtered alike, and the card's filtering at a slant brings them to 24%. The bound stays as
it is in this commit, and the job's commit bounds the filtering's share apart, 25% on a device whose
filtering at a slant darkens the leaves as the card's does and 29% on a CPU device, whose filtering
leaves them as one sample does, where lavapipe read 27.7% in the trial and 27.8% in the read.

ThunderTests.AStrikeLightsTheNightAndDrawsItsBolt failed, the strike not lighting the ground. The
flash dies away over half a second of Time.Delta, and the test waits four frames before its lit
picture, which on lavapipe took 0.55 seconds of the machine's clock, so the test read the machine's
clock in effect, as N 3.3 bars. It runs on a set frame time of a sixtieth of a second. As it was,
the test passed on lavapipe at four cores in one run of two and failed at one core, and mended it
passes at one core and on the card.

CaptureTests.WhatWasDrawnCanBeReadBack read its red channel as 0 once, on the first whole run's cold
cache, and passed on the clean pass. It asked for its capture at frame 10 whatever its pipelines'
state, and the camera draws nothing into its target until they are ready. It asks once every
pipeline has been ready three frames running, as PictureRun.Capture does, and the app runs until the
picture arrives. From a Mesa cache that started empty the test as it was read its red channel as 0
again, and mended it asked for its capture at frame 42 and passed.

The job is planned by these minutes. A part holds at most 38 minutes here, which the slowest Linux
runner read, an EPYC 7763 drawing about 1.1 times as slowly as this container, takes in 42, under
the 45. A class goes whole into a part where it fits one and by its cases where it does not, as
global illumination's, the bounce rooms', the reference's and the trees' leaves and levels do, first
fit from the longest. Every class comes to 13 full parts and a sliver, 494 minutes of the runners'
time, 271 of them the 22 cases of five minutes or more, each a reading against a traced reference, a
forest or a tree between its levels. All of them run on every push, the long cases among them, laid
out by wall time, a part a job where the account's concurrent jobs allow it beside the build's other
legs and two a job where they would queue each other, and the three cases past 41 minutes run on the
card alone, skipped on a CPU device with the reason said where they are skipped, as the seven
readings of a cost are. build/test.py has --parts and --filter and no way to name a part, so that
commit gives it one, as the sibling's --split and --only do, and a bound that moves on lavapipe is
said there as a count of pixels with its reason.

Shared: lavapipe in Mesa 25.2.8 meets nothing in a ray scene's instance laid after one of mask zero,
and its filtering at a slant leaves a texture as one sample does where a card's sixteen samples

146's medium findings 32, 37 and 38, the session file, a panic that ends the run and a canceled
read, in the commit carrying this Reply, each with a test that failed without its mend.

The session file is opened anew with the owner's read and write alone from the moment it is made,
before the token goes into it, a temporary file a crashed write left deleted first, and the sessions
folder is made the owner's alone where it is missing, where the file was made under the process's
umask, 0644 here, and its mode set only once the token was in it, and the folder made 0755. A folder
that is there keeps its mode, since BCS_SESSIONS may name one somebody else made.
CliSessionTests.TheTokenIsNeverWhereAnotherAccountCouldReadIt reads the file's mode as the token is
about to go in, through a call CliSessionFile makes for a test, and the folder's once it is written.
Without the mend the token went into a file of mode 0644, which the group and others read, and with
it the file is its owner's alone as the token goes in and so is the folder.

A panic on the main thread inside Bevy's run, which the guard around the run hears as the bridge's
status and the hook leaves unwritten, is written to the crash file whole and thrown from App.Run as
a BevyNativeException, where the status went back as the code the process ends with.
CrashLogTests.APanicThatEndsTheRunIsWrittenAndThrown runs an app for two frames through the bridge's
run followed by a panic inside the guard, the bridge's own panic made on purpose, which stands for
one that unwinds out of Bevy's run as the bridge's status and its last panic. Without the mend the
run handed back the bridge's status and threw nothing, and with it the run throws the panic's words
and the crash file holds them under a heading of their own.

A streamed read keeps what it brought back only while it is not canceled, under a lock
Streaming.Cancel takes to drop a finished read, so a read canceled while its file read ran, or
before a slice too short to read was kept, never lands after its cancel.
StreamingTests.ACanceledReadNeverLandsAfterItsCancel asks for eight empty slices at a priority of 1,
canceling each as it is asked for, and then a read at 0. Without the mend 7 of the 8 canceled reads
landed after their cancel, and with it none does and the read at 0 is handed over.

The whole suite that passed over these mends is the one 143's Reply above gives. NormTests passed,
